This page lists every current scalar, list, and map in chart defaults, checked-in overlays, GitOps values and manifests, release values, and infrastructure manifests. Each field row separates the checked-in source from the runtime receiver. It follows local Helm templates, Argo CD value-file bindings, and Kubernetes resource authorities. An external chart or Kubernetes API owns validation when its schema is outside this repository. A field with no active deployment binding is identified as inactive instead of being presented as an effective option.

| `$.busterNamespaceBroker.allowedPrefixes` | Defines the namespace-name prefixes shared by the namespace controller, its admission fence, and the namespace-lease CRD. Accepted values: Use a deliberate nonempty list of valid namespace-name prefixes, such as &#91;&#34;test&#34;&#93;. The controller matches prefix plus &#34;-&#34;; the CRD enum restricts spec.namespacePrefix when that optional field is supplied. Selected chart default: the checked-in value in this row is the chart default. Empty or omitted value: Omission keeps the earlier list; a later &#91;&#93; replaces it with no items. All three templates render only when busterNamespaceBroker.enabled is true and agentRole is buster; the fence also requires Kubernetes &#62;=1.30. An omitted override retains the merged list. An effective &#91;&#93; renders an empty controller environment string, &#91;&#93;.exists(prefix, ...) in the Fail/Deny fence, and enum: &#91;&#93; in the lease CRD. The controller falls back to test and the fence cannot match any namespace name. The CRD renders enum: &#91;&#93;, but the pinned Kubernetes validator checks enum values only when that list is nonempty, so this empty enum adds no restriction on namespacePrefix; the remaining schema and admission rules still apply. Validator proof: &#91;CRD enum conversion&#93;(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/66452049f3d692768c39c797b21b793dce80314e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/validation/validation.go#L293-L298), &#91;enum consumer&#93;(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/66452049f3d692768c39c797b21b793dce80314e/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/schema.go#L197-L203), and &#91;nonempty-enum validation&#93;(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/66452049f3d692768c39c797b21b793dce80314e/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/validator.go#L56-L71). Explicit null renders null.exists(prefix, ...) and a null enum; neither template uses the controller fallback. Null is not a supported recovery value. | Item child `icmps` | ICMPs is a list of ICMP rule identified by type number<br>which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to connect to.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=httpd&#34; is allowed to initiate<br>type 8 ICMP connections.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toCIDR` | ToCIDR is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the rule<br>is allowed to initiate connections. Only connections destined for<br>outside of the cluster and not targeting the host will be subject<br>to CIDR rules.  This will match on the destination IP address of<br>outgoing connections. Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet<br>with no ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between<br>ToCIDR and ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toCIDRSet` | ToCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the rule<br>is allowed to initiate connections to in addition to connections<br>which are allowed via ToEndpoints, along with a list of subnets contained<br>within their corresponding IP block to which traffic should not be<br>allowed. This will match on the destination IP address of outgoing<br>connections. Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet with no<br>ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between ToCIDR and<br>ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24 except from IPs in subnet 10.2.3.0/28.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toEndpoints` | ToEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an EndpointSelector to<br>which the endpoints subject to the rule are allowed to communicate.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; can communicate with any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=backend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil ToEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil ToEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toEntities` | ToEntities is a list of special entities to which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to initiate connections. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toFQDNs` | ToFQDN allows whitelisting DNS names in place of IPs. The IPs that result<br>from DNS resolution of &#96;ToFQDN.MatchName&#96;s are added to the same<br>EgressRule object as ToCIDRSet entries, and behave accordingly. Any L4 and<br>L7 rules within this EgressRule will also apply to these IPs.<br>The DNS -&#62; IP mapping is re-resolved periodically from within the<br>cilium-agent, and the IPs in the DNS response are effected in the policy<br>for selected pods as-is (i.e. the list of IPs is not modified in any way).<br>Note: An explicit rule to allow for DNS traffic is needed for the pods, as<br>ToFQDN counts as an egress rule and will enforce egress policy when<br>PolicyEnforcment=default.<br>Note: If the resolved IPs are IPs within the kubernetes cluster, the<br>ToFQDN rule will not apply to that IP.<br>Note: ToFQDN cannot occur in the same policy as other To&#42; rules.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>toGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Item child `toPorts` | ToPorts is a list of destination ports identified by port number and<br>protocol which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to<br>connect to.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; is allowed to initiate<br>connections to destination port 8080/tcp<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

Only connections destined for<br>outside of the cluster and not targeting the host will be subject<br>to CIDR rules.  This will match on the destination IP address of<br>outgoing connections. Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet<br>with no ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between<br>ToCIDR and ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toCIDRSet` | ToCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the rule<br>is allowed to initiate connections to in addition to connections<br>which are allowed via ToEndpoints, along with a list of subnets contained<br>within their corresponding IP block to which traffic should not be<br>allowed. This will match on the destination IP address of outgoing<br>connections. Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet with no<br>ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between ToCIDR and<br>ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24 except from IPs in subnet 10.2.3.0/28.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toEndpoints` | ToEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an EndpointSelector to<br>which the endpoints subject to the rule are allowed to communicate.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; can communicate with any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=backend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil ToEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil ToEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toEntities` | ToEntities is a list of special entities to which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to initiate connections. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toFQDNs` | ToFQDN allows whitelisting DNS names in place of IPs. The IPs that result<br>from DNS resolution of &#96;ToFQDN.MatchName&#96;s are added to the same<br>EgressRule object as ToCIDRSet entries, and behave accordingly. Any L4 and<br>L7 rules within this EgressRule will also apply to these IPs.<br>The DNS -&#62; IP mapping is re-resolved periodically from within the<br>cilium-agent, and the IPs in the DNS response are effected in the policy<br>for selected pods as-is (i.e. the list of IPs is not modified in any way).<br>Note: An explicit rule to allow for DNS traffic is needed for the pods, as<br>ToFQDN counts as an egress rule and will enforce egress policy when<br>PolicyEnforcment=default.<br>Note: If the resolved IPs are IPs within the kubernetes cluster, the<br>ToFQDN rule will not apply to that IP.<br>Note: ToFQDN cannot occur in the same policy as other To&#42; rules.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toGroups` | ToGroups allows policies to reference CIDRs provided by external integrations.<br>Currently, only AWS is supported, and the rule can select by multiple sub directives.<br>ToGroups entries are functionally equivalent to toCIDR, and have the same<br>limitiations. They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>toGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toNodes` | ToNodes is a list of nodes identified by an<br>EndpointSelector to which endpoints subject to the rule is allowed to communicate.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toPorts` | ToPorts is a list of destination ports identified by port number and<br>protocol which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to<br>connect to.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; is allowed to initiate<br>connections to destination port 8080/tcp<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Boundary | Exact schema contract |

| Field | EnableDefaultDeny determines whether this policy configures the<br>subject endpoint(s) to have a default deny mode. If enabled,<br>this causes all traffic not explicitly allowed by a network policy<br>to be dropped.<br><br>If not specified, the default is true for each traffic direction<br>that has rules, and false otherwise. For example, if a policy<br>only has Ingress or IngressDeny rules, then the default for<br>ingress is true and egress is false.<br><br>If multiple policies apply to an endpoint, that endpoint&#39;s default deny<br>will be enabled if any policy requests it.<br><br>This is useful for creating broad-based network policies that will not<br>cause endpoints to enter default-deny mode.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Boundary | Exact schema contract |

| Field | Ingress is a list of IngressRule which are enforced at ingress.<br>If omitted or empty, this rule does not apply at ingress.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| List item | IngressRule contains all rule types which can be applied at ingress,<br>i.e. network traffic that originates outside of the endpoint and<br>is entering the endpoint selected by the endpointSelector.<br><br>  - All members of this structure are optional. If omitted or empty, the<br>    member will have no effect on the rule.<br><br>  - If multiple members are set, all of them need to match in order for<br>    the rule to take effect.<br><br>  - FromEndpoints, FromCIDR, FromCIDRSet and FromEntities are mutually<br>    exclusive. Only one of these members may be present within an individual<br>    rule.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Map value | This field has no contract at this boundary. |
| Item child `authentication` | Authentication is the required authentication type for the allowed traffic, if any.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;mode&#34;&#93;,&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;required&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromCIDR` | FromCIDR is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from. Only connections which<br>do &#42;not&#42; originate from the cluster or from the local host are subject<br>to CIDR rules. In order to allow in-cluster connectivity, use the<br>FromEndpoints field.  This will match on the source IP address of<br>incoming connections. Adding  a prefix into FromCIDR or into<br>FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is  equivalent.  Overlaps are<br>allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.3.9.1<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromCIDRSet` | FromCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from in addition to FromEndpoints,<br>along with a list of subnets contained within their corresponding IP block<br>from which traffic should not be allowed.<br>This will match on the source IP address of incoming connections. Adding<br>a prefix into FromCIDR or into FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is<br>equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.0.0.0/8 except from IPs in subnet 10.96.0.0/12.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromEndpoints` | FromEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an<br>EndpointSelector which are allowed to communicate with the endpoint<br>subject to the rule.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=backend&#34; can be consumed by any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=frontend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil FromEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil FromEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromEntities` | FromEntities is a list of special entities which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to receive connections from. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromGroups` | FromGroups allows policies to reference CIDRs provided by external integrations.<br>Currently, only AWS is supported, and the rule can select by multiple sub directives.<br>FromGroups entries are functionally equivalent to FromCIDR, and have the same<br>limitiations. They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>fromGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromNodes` | FromNodes is a list of nodes identified by an<br>EndpointSelector which are allowed to communicate with the endpoint<br>subject to the rule.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Child `fromCIDR` | FromCIDR is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from. Only connections which<br>do &#42;not&#42; originate from the cluster or from the local host are subject<br>to CIDR rules. In order to allow in-cluster connectivity, use the<br>FromEndpoints field.  This will match on the source IP address of<br>incoming connections. Adding  a prefix into FromCIDR or into<br>FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is  equivalent.  Overlaps are<br>allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.3.9.1<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `fromCIDRSet` | FromCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from in addition to FromEndpoints,<br>along with a list of subnets contained within their corresponding IP block<br>from which traffic should not be allowed.<br>This will match on the source IP address of incoming connections. Adding<br>a prefix into FromCIDR or into FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is<br>equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.0.0.0/8 except from IPs in subnet 10.96.0.0/12.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `fromEndpoints` | FromEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an<br>EndpointSelector which are allowed to communicate with the endpoint<br>subject to the rule.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=backend&#34; can be consumed by any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=frontend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil FromEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil FromEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `fromEntities` | FromEntities is a list of special entities which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to receive connections from. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>fromGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

If omitted or empty, the<br>    member will have no effect on the rule.<br><br>  - If multiple members of the structure are specified, then all members<br>    must match in order for the rule to take effect.<br><br>  - ToEndpoints, ToCIDR, ToCIDRSet, ToEntities, ToServices and ToGroups are<br>    mutually exclusive. Only one of these members may be present within an<br>    individual rule.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Map value | This field has no contract at this boundary. |
| Item child `authentication` | Authentication is the required authentication type for the allowed traffic, if any.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;mode&#34;&#93;,&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;required&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `icmps` | ICMPs is a list of ICMP rule identified by type number<br>which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to connect to.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=httpd&#34; is allowed to initiate<br>type 8 ICMP connections.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toCIDR` | ToCIDR is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the rule<br>is allowed to initiate connections. Only connections destined for<br>outside of the cluster and not targeting the host will be subject<br>to CIDR rules.  This will match on the destination IP address of<br>outgoing connections. Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet<br>with no ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between<br>ToCIDR and ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toCIDRSet` | ToCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the rule<br>is allowed to initiate connections to in addition to connections<br>which are allowed via ToEndpoints, along with a list of subnets contained<br>within their corresponding IP block to which traffic should not be<br>allowed. This will match on the destination IP address of outgoing<br>connections. Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet with no<br>ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between ToCIDR and<br>ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24 except from IPs in subnet 10.2.3.0/28.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toEndpoints` | ToEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an EndpointSelector to<br>which the endpoints subject to the rule are allowed to communicate.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; can communicate with any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=backend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil ToEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil ToEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toEntities` | ToEntities is a list of special entities to which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to initiate connections. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toFQDNs` | ToFQDN allows whitelisting DNS names in place of IPs. The IPs that result<br>from DNS resolution of &#96;ToFQDN.MatchName&#96;s are added to the same<br>EgressRule object as ToCIDRSet entries, and behave accordingly. Any L4 and<br>L7 rules within this EgressRule will also apply to these IPs.<br>The DNS -&#62; IP mapping is re-resolved periodically from within the<br>cilium-agent, and the IPs in the DNS response are effected in the policy<br>for selected pods as-is (i.e. the list of IPs is not modified in any way).<br>Note: An explicit rule to allow for DNS traffic is needed for the pods, as<br>ToFQDN counts as an egress rule and will enforce egress policy when<br>PolicyEnforcment=default.<br>Note: If the resolved IPs are IPs within the kubernetes cluster, the<br>ToFQDN rule will not apply to that IP.<br>Note: ToFQDN cannot occur in the same policy as other To&#42; rules.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toGroups` | ToGroups allows policies to reference CIDRs provided by external integrations.<br>Currently, only AWS is supported, and the rule can select by multiple sub directives.<br>ToGroups entries are functionally equivalent to toCIDR, and have the same<br>limitiations. They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>toGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toNodes` | ToNodes is a list of nodes identified by an<br>EndpointSelector to which endpoints subject to the rule is allowed to communicate.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toPorts` | ToPorts is a list of destination ports identified by port number and<br>protocol which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to<br>connect to.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; is allowed to initiate<br>connections to destination port 8080/tcp<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Item child `toServices` | ToServices is a list of services to which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to initiate connections.<br>Currently Cilium only supports toServices for K8s services.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Boundary | Exact schema contract |

| Child `icmps` | ICMPs is a list of ICMP rule identified by type number<br>which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to connect to.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=httpd&#34; is allowed to initiate<br>type 8 ICMP connections.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet<br>with no ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between<br>ToCIDR and ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toCIDRSet` | ToCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the rule<br>is allowed to initiate connections to in addition to connections<br>which are allowed via ToEndpoints, along with a list of subnets contained<br>within their corresponding IP block to which traffic should not be<br>allowed. This will match on the destination IP address of outgoing<br>connections. Adding a prefix into ToCIDR or into ToCIDRSet with no<br>ExcludeCIDRs is equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between ToCIDR and<br>ToCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=database-proxy&#34; is allowed to<br>initiate connections to 10.2.3.0/24 except from IPs in subnet 10.2.3.0/28.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toEndpoints` | ToEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an EndpointSelector to<br>which the endpoints subject to the rule are allowed to communicate.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; can communicate with any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=backend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil ToEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil ToEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toEntities` | ToEntities is a list of special entities to which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to initiate connections. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toFQDNs` | ToFQDN allows whitelisting DNS names in place of IPs. The IPs that result<br>from DNS resolution of &#96;ToFQDN.MatchName&#96;s are added to the same<br>EgressRule object as ToCIDRSet entries, and behave accordingly. Any L4 and<br>L7 rules within this EgressRule will also apply to these IPs.<br>The DNS -&#62; IP mapping is re-resolved periodically from within the<br>cilium-agent, and the IPs in the DNS response are effected in the policy<br>for selected pods as-is (i.e. the list of IPs is not modified in any way).<br>Note: An explicit rule to allow for DNS traffic is needed for the pods, as<br>ToFQDN counts as an egress rule and will enforce egress policy when<br>PolicyEnforcment=default.<br>Note: If the resolved IPs are IPs within the kubernetes cluster, the<br>ToFQDN rule will not apply to that IP.<br>Note: ToFQDN cannot occur in the same policy as other To&#42; rules.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toGroups` | ToGroups allows policies to reference CIDRs provided by external integrations.<br>Currently, only AWS is supported, and the rule can select by multiple sub directives.<br>ToGroups entries are functionally equivalent to toCIDR, and have the same<br>limitiations. They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>toGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toNodes` | ToNodes is a list of nodes identified by an<br>EndpointSelector to which endpoints subject to the rule is allowed to communicate.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `toPorts` | ToPorts is a list of destination ports identified by port number and<br>protocol which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to<br>connect to.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=frontend&#34; is allowed to initiate<br>connections to destination port 8080/tcp<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

This section preserves the exact pinned schema descriptions. It describes accepted shape and the stated API behavior. A missing schema default does not prove that the controller inserts no default. A patch annotation does not select the client's apply mode.

| Boundary | Exact schema contract |
| --- | --- |
| Field | EnableDefaultDeny determines whether this policy configures the<br>subject endpoint(s) to have a default deny mode. If enabled,<br>this causes all traffic not explicitly allowed by a network policy<br>to be dropped.<br><br>If not specified, the default is true for each traffic direction<br>that has rules, and false otherwise. For example, if a policy<br>only has Ingress or IngressDeny rules, then the default for<br>ingress is true and egress is false.<br><br>If multiple policies apply to an endpoint, that endpoint&#39;s default deny<br>will be enabled if any policy requests it.<br><br>This is useful for creating broad-based network policies that will not<br>cause endpoints to enter default-deny mode.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| List item | This field has no contract at this boundary. |
| Map value | This field has no contract at this boundary. |
| Child `egress` | Whether or not the endpoint should have a default-deny rule applied<br>to egress traffic.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;boolean&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `ingress` | Whether or not the endpoint should have a default-deny rule applied<br>to ingress traffic.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;boolean&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Parent `<API object>` | CiliumNetworkPolicy is a Kubernetes third-party resource with an extended<br>version of NetworkPolicy.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;path&#34;:&#34;&#34;,&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;metadata&#34;&#93;,&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-validations&#34;:&#91;{&#34;message&#34;:&#34;spec or specs must be provided&#34;,&#34;rule&#34;:&#34;has(self.spec) &#124;&#124; has(self.specs)&#34;}&#93;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;required&#34;,&#34;type&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-validations&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Parent `spec` | Spec is the desired Cilium specific rule specification.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;anyOf&#34;:&#91;{&#34;properties&#34;:{&#34;ingress&#34;:{}},&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;ingress&#34;&#93;},{&#34;properties&#34;:{&#34;ingressDeny&#34;:{}},&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;ingressDeny&#34;&#93;},{&#34;properties&#34;:{&#34;egress&#34;:{}},&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;egress&#34;&#93;},{&#34;properties&#34;:{&#34;egressDeny&#34;:{}},&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;egressDeny&#34;&#93;}&#93;,&#34;oneOf&#34;:&#91;{&#34;properties&#34;:{&#34;endpointSelector&#34;:{}},&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;endpointSelector&#34;&#93;},{&#34;properties&#34;:{&#34;nodeSelector&#34;:{}},&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;nodeSelector&#34;&#93;}&#93;,&#34;path&#34;:&#34;spec&#34;,&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;anyOf&#34;,&#34;description&#34;,&#34;oneOf&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

### CiliumNetworkPolicy: <code>spec.ingress</code>

Authority: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cilium/cilium/v1.20.1/pkg/k8s/apis/cilium.io/client/crds/v2/ciliumnetworkpolicies.yaml. Content SHA-256: `62c6de8f358da125b94468d39187edb1cea157d79503fdc50ccec8a6aaa79a76`. API: `cilium.io/v2/CiliumNetworkPolicy`.

This section preserves the exact pinned schema descriptions. It describes accepted shape and the stated API behavior. Read the linked field row for the selected input, actual apply or loader receiver, operational consequence, and controller limit. A missing schema default does not prove that the controller inserts no default. A patch annotation does not select the client's apply mode.

| Boundary | Exact schema contract |
| --- | --- |
| Field | Ingress is a list of IngressRule which are enforced at ingress.<br>If omitted or empty, this rule does not apply at ingress.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| List item | IngressRule contains all rule types which can be applied at ingress,<br>i.e. network traffic that originates outside of the endpoint and<br>is entering the endpoint selected by the endpointSelector.<br><br>  - All members of this structure are optional. If omitted or empty, the<br>    member will have no effect on the rule.<br><br>  - If multiple members are set, all of them need to match in order for<br>    the rule to take effect.<br><br>  - FromEndpoints, FromCIDR, FromCIDRSet and FromEntities are mutually<br>    exclusive. Only one of these members may be present within an individual<br>    rule.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Map value | This field has no contract at this boundary. |
| Item child `authentication` | Authentication is the required authentication type for the allowed traffic, if any.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;required&#34;:&#91;&#34;mode&#34;&#93;,&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;required&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromCIDR` | FromCIDR is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from. Only connections which<br>do &#42;not&#42; originate from the cluster or from the local host are subject<br>to CIDR rules. In order to allow in-cluster connectivity, use the<br>FromEndpoints field.  This will match on the source IP address of<br>incoming connections. Adding  a prefix into FromCIDR or into<br>FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is  equivalent.  Overlaps are<br>allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.3.9.1<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromCIDRSet` | FromCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from in addition to FromEndpoints,<br>along with a list of subnets contained within their corresponding IP block<br>from which traffic should not be allowed.<br>This will match on the source IP address of incoming connections. Adding<br>a prefix into FromCIDR or into FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is<br>equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.0.0.0/8 except from IPs in subnet 10.96.0.0/12.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromEndpoints` | FromEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an<br>EndpointSelector which are allowed to communicate with the endpoint<br>subject to the rule.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=backend&#34; can be consumed by any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=frontend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil FromEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil FromEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromEntities` | FromEntities is a list of special entities which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to receive connections from. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromGroups` | FromGroups allows policies to reference CIDRs provided by external integrations.<br>Currently, only AWS is supported, and the rule can select by multiple sub directives.<br>FromGroups entries are functionally equivalent to FromCIDR, and have the same<br>limitiations. They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>fromGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromNodes` | FromNodes is a list of nodes identified by an<br>EndpointSelector which are allowed to communicate with the endpoint<br>subject to the rule.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `fromRequires` | Deprecated.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;maxItems&#34;:0,&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;maxItems&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `icmps` | ICMPs is a list of ICMP rule identified by type number<br>which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to<br>receive connections on.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=httpd&#34; can only accept incoming<br>type 8 ICMP connections.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Item child `toPorts` | ToPorts is a list of destination ports identified by port number and<br>protocol which the endpoint subject to the rule is allowed to<br>receive connections on.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=httpd&#34; can only accept incoming<br>connections on port 80/tcp.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

If omitted or empty, the<br>    member will have no effect on the rule.<br><br>  - If multiple members are set, all of them need to match in order for<br>    the rule to take effect.<br><br>  - FromEndpoints, FromCIDR, FromCIDRSet and FromEntities are mutually<br>    exclusive. Only one of these members may be present within an individual<br>    rule.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;object&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;properties&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Child `fromCIDR` | FromCIDR is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from. Only connections which<br>do &#42;not&#42; originate from the cluster or from the local host are subject<br>to CIDR rules. In order to allow in-cluster connectivity, use the<br>FromEndpoints field.  This will match on the source IP address of<br>incoming connections. Adding  a prefix into FromCIDR or into<br>FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is  equivalent.  Overlaps are<br>allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.3.9.1<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `fromCIDRSet` | FromCIDRSet is a list of IP blocks which the endpoint subject to the<br>rule is allowed to receive connections from in addition to FromEndpoints,<br>along with a list of subnets contained within their corresponding IP block<br>from which traffic should not be allowed.<br>This will match on the source IP address of incoming connections. Adding<br>a prefix into FromCIDR or into FromCIDRSet with no ExcludeCIDRs is<br>equivalent. Overlaps are allowed between FromCIDR and FromCIDRSet.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;app=my-legacy-pet&#34; is allowed to receive<br>connections from 10.0.0.0/8 except from IPs in subnet 10.96.0.0/12.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `fromEndpoints` | FromEndpoints is a list of endpoints identified by an<br>EndpointSelector which are allowed to communicate with the endpoint<br>subject to the rule.<br><br>Example:<br>Any endpoint with the label &#34;role=backend&#34; can be consumed by any<br>endpoint carrying the label &#34;role=frontend&#34;.<br><br>Note that while an empty non-nil FromEndpoints does not select anything,<br>nil FromEndpoints is implicitly treated as a wildcard selector if ToPorts<br>are also specified.<br>To select everything, use one EndpointSelector without any match requirements.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |
| Child `fromEntities` | FromEntities is a list of special entities which the endpoint subject<br>to the rule is allowed to receive connections from. Supported entities are<br>&#96;world&#96;, &#96;cluster&#96;, &#96;cluster-mesh&#96;, &#96;host&#96;, &#96;remote-node&#96;, &#96;kube-apiserver&#96;, &#96;ingress&#96;, &#96;init&#96;,<br>&#96;health&#96;, &#96;unmanaged&#96;, &#96;none&#96; and &#96;all&#96;.<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

They cannot select traffic originating from within the cluster.<br><br>Example:<br>fromGroups:<br>- aws:<br>    securityGroupsIds:<br>    - &#39;sg-XXXXXXXXXXXXX&#39;<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;&#93;</code> |

| Boundary | Exact schema contract |
| --- | --- |
| Field | MatchConditions is a list of conditions that must be met for a request to be validated. Match conditions filter requests that have already been matched by the rules, namespaceSelector, and objectSelector. An empty list of matchConditions matches all requests. There are a maximum of 64 match conditions allowed.<br><br>If a parameter object is provided, it can be accessed via the &#96;params&#96; handle in the same manner as validation expressions.<br><br>The exact matching logic is (in order):<br>  1. If ANY matchCondition evaluates to FALSE, the policy is skipped.<br>  2. If ALL matchConditions evaluate to TRUE, the policy is evaluated.<br>  3. If any matchCondition evaluates to an error (but none are FALSE):<br>     - If failurePolicy=Fail, reject the request<br>     - If failurePolicy=Ignore, the policy is skipped<br>Constraints and alternatives: <code>{&#34;type&#34;:&#34;array&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-list-map-keys&#34;:&#91;&#34;name&#34;&#93;,&#34;x-kubernetes-list-type&#34;:&#34;map&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-patch-merge-key&#34;:&#34;name&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-patch-strategy&#34;:&#34;merge&#34;}</code><br>Keywords at this boundary: <code>&#91;&#34;description&#34;,&#34;items&#34;,&#34;type&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-list-map-keys&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-list-type&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-patch-merge-key&#34;,&#34;x-kubernetes-patch-strategy&#34;&#93;</code> |

### ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding: <code>spec.validationActions</code>

Authority: Kubernetes v1.35.0 OpenAPI io.k8s.api.admissionregistration.v1.ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding. Content SHA-256: `483500149ee52ce5753d75f5639101d985bb4f5e902cc05b1ba7627465d62446`. API: `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding`.

This section preserves the exact pinned schema descriptions. It describes accepted shape and the stated API behavior. Read the linked field row for the selected input, actual apply or loader receiver, operational consequence, and controller limit. A missing schema default does not prove that the controller inserts no default. A patch annotation does not select the client's apply mode.

| Boundary | Exact schema contract |
| --- | --- |
| Field | validationActions declares how Validations of the referenced ValidatingAdmissionPolicy are enforced. If a validation evaluates to false it is always enforced according to these actions.<br><br>Failures defined by the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy&#39;s FailurePolicy are enforced according to these actions only if the FailurePolicy is set to Fail, otherwise the failures are ignored. This includes compilation errors, runtime errors and misconfigurations of the policy.<br><br>validationActions is declared as a set of action values. | Field | policyTypes is a list of rule types that the NetworkPolicy relates to. Valid options are &#91;&#34;Ingress&#34;&#93;, &#91;&#34;Egress&#34;&#93;, or &#91;&#34;Ingress&#34;, &#34;Egress&#34;&#93;. If this field is not specified, it will default based on the existence of ingress or egress rules; policies that contain an egress section are assumed to affect egress, and all policies (whether or not they contain an ingress section) are assumed to affect ingress. If you want to write an egress-only policy, you must explicitly specify policyTypes &#91; &#34;Egress&#34; &#93;. Likewise, if you want to write a policy that specifies that no egress is allowed, you must specify a policyTypes value that include &#34;Egress&#34; (since such a policy would not include an egress section and would otherwise default to just &#91; &#34;Ingress&#34; &#93;). ## Deployed Configuration Payloads

The chart embeds each file below in the swarm ConfigMap and the init process materializes it in runtime configuration. YAML and JSON files are expanded to every leaf. Executable JavaScript and HCL files remain complete, digest-pinned files because treating their syntax as ordinary key/value data would invent semantics. A payload without a checked-in reader is identified as tool- or image-owned.

Source selection and retention:

Mounted chart bytes replace the persistent file only when OVERRIDE_SWARM_CONFIG is true or the persistent file is absent. Otherwise the existing persistent file wins. The runtime copy uses the resulting persistent file.

- [`charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:634`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/6fa4830a48244d29655104a5be58957d5fa87d2f/charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml#L634-L634) — the chart source participates only when the mounted .semgrep.yml exists.
- [`charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:635`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/6fa4830a48244d29655104a5be58957d5fa87d2f/charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml#L635-L635) — chart bytes replace persistent .semgrep.yml only when override is true or no persistent file exists.
- [`charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml:639`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/6fa4830a48244d29655104a5be58957d5fa87d2f/charts/kubeclaw/templates/deployment.yaml#L639-L639) — an existing persistent .semgrep.yml is retained when override is false.

## Runtime Meaning

| Value group | Runtime effect | Expected proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| image and pull secrets | selects agent and sidecar images, tags, pull policy, and GHCR pull Secret | rendered Deployments include expected image refs and `imagePullSecrets` |
| auth/provider/Discord/Stitch/LiteLLM | selects direct values or existing Secret name/key references | rendered env refs point to expected Secret keys and generated secrets reference lists those keys |
| persistence | creates workspace/config PVCs for gateway and plugin-runtime state | rendered PVCs and security contexts match production values |
| service and extra ports | exposes gateway/bridge ClusterIP ports plus explicit extra NodePorts | rendered Services contain only documented ports |
| buster namespace broker | adds lease CRD/RBAC/controller and controller env vars | Buster render includes CRD, lease client RBAC, controller Deployment, and namespace fence docs |
| probes, startup doctor, and dependency checks | configures gateway, Redis, and LiteLLM health checks; `gateway.startupDoctor` runs `openclaw doctor --fix` as a blocking state update while the gateway is stopped | rendered init container, env vars, and smoke commands exercise the health and doctor surfaces |

## Failure Signals

- A top-level value appears in this page but has no rendered effect: add deployment truth coverage or remove the stale value.
- Rendered Secret refs do not match `my-values/setup-secrets.sh`: update values, helper, inventory, and docs together.
- Buster values disable sandbox/broker behavior unexpectedly: inspect `my-values/buster-values.yaml` before changing chart templates.
- A live pod keeps old config after values change: remember the init container preserves persisted config unless override flags request replacement.
